beat_player.text: {troop_count} troops and no flank. Your line folded on the second charge, {player}. Fix the spacing.
Wrong, {player}. Your reserve sat idle for six minutes. Idle troops are the cheapest loss there is. gg.
Good fight, {player}. Your flank timing slipped at the ford and cost you {troop_count} men. My push landed on schedule. Sort the spacing next time and you will be dangerous.

beat_by_player.text: My archers were out of position on that flank, {player}. Lost {troop_count} to a timing error. That is not the same as losing the fight.
Your push came in 40 seconds early by my count, {player}. I had the timing right and the positioning wrong. Rematch when I fix it.
Clean fight, {player}. I lost {troop_count} to a flank I should have covered. My spreadsheet says the gap was three ranks wide. I will close it before the next siege.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. {troop_count} troops and a spreadsheet full of gaps. Counting this as a grudge now.
That is the third time, {player}. I have the logs. The timing is sound, so the flank is where I will find the gap.
Third loss to you, {player}. Honest read: you read my line better than I read yours. I am still correcting the ratios.

player_win_streak.text: {player} is on a streak and everyone keeps saying luck. It is not luck. Look at the flank timing and stop calling it chance.
Your streak is real, {player}. Most of it is ratio discipline, the rest is you not overextending. I respect the discipline.
Keep it up, {player}. Streaks break on the flank, and I have a fix for you if you want it.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of the army and is calling it bad luck. The flank was empty and the reserve came too late. Fix it.
Rough day, {player}. {troop_count} troops gone to a unit sent into a corner. Send your archers wider next time.
Bad field, {player}. The math still says your army was sound. Tell me what went wrong and I will tell you what I would have done.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}, meet me at {village} at dawn with equal numbers. I have the timing worked out. Clean terms, no excuses.
{player}, you owe me a clean field. Meet at {town} before noon. I bring the spreadsheet, you bring the archers.
{player}, {town} is open ground with a clean approach. Meet me there. I want to test the gap I found in your last formation.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} held the ridge while my second line closed on {enemy_faction}. Good ratio, {troop_count} men, clean finish.
Nice work on the flank, {player}. The timing held and your line did not break. Good to have you on my side for once.
We split {enemy_faction} clean, {player}. {troop_count} men on the line and not one caught out of position. Do the same at the next siege and we keep this ratio.

ambient_brag.text: {fief} garrison is at {troop_count} men and {gold} gold in the coffers. Efficient, as always. Not bragging, just reporting.
Ran the numbers on the last siege. {troop_count} men, {fief} taken before dawn, costs under budget. The spreadsheet is never wrong.
{gold} gold and {troop_count} troops, with no wasted ranks. Anyone still fielding a loose line is paying for it.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours. {my_faction} took it from {enemy_faction} before dawn with the flank timed to the second. Clean capture.
Captured {fief} for {my_faction}. Their reserve was three ranks late. Nothing to talk about, the numbers did the work.
{fief} changed hands. {my_faction} push came in on schedule, {enemy_faction} did not expect it. Ratios favored us from the start.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} is sieging {fief}. Check the walls, the approach has a gap on the east side. Try not to waste it, {player}.
{player}, you started a siege on {fief} with the wrong ratio. I have the numbers. Lift it before you lose the men.
Siege on {fief}, {player}. I will hold it. Come back when your ratios are better and I will show you where the wall fails.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Bad for archers, good for the slow ones. Nothing to fix about that.
Lag at {village} is killing the flank timing. Someone should look at the server before the next siege.
Anyone else notice the map pins near {village} are off by a tile? Spreadsheet says the road is shorter than we think.
